---
title: "From data to posterior decisions"
subtitle: "1.7 · after Walters (Mixtape slides) and Kline, Rose and Walters (2024)"
description: "Separation of model fitting, posterior calculation and grade-report selection."
---

An analyst fits a model and prior to data $Y$ to obtain $\Pr(\theta \mid Y)$; `postrank` acts only at the final step, turning that supplied posterior into grades.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Box 1 (Data).** $Y$ holds `.25` (SE `.10`) for A and `.05` (SE `.20`) for B.
- **Box 2 (Model).** Prior SD `.15` keeps `.692` of A's estimate and `.360` of B's.
- **Box 3 (Posterior).** Means `.173` and `.0180` give $\pi = .856$; **B more precise** (SE `.10`) keeps `.692`, raising B to `.0346` and $\pi$ to `.880`.
- **Box 4 (Decision).** `{A} > {B}` costs `.144` vs. $\tau = .20$ (`best of all 3 reports`); **τ .10** withholds `{A, B}`.
- **Prior SD .05.** Shrinks A to `.0500` and $\pi$ to `.762` (error `.238`), withholding `{A, B}`.

<details>
<summary>Source notes (Walters; Kline, Rose and Walters, 2024)</summary>

Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section III.A–B, set out the empirical Bayes posteriors behind their firm grades (KRW call them beliefs). In their talk, slides 34 and 37 show the model for first names, not for the firms; slides 43 to 52 set out the empirical Bayes model for the firms. Walters' Mixtape slides on empirical Bayes (p. 13) set out the same recipe. The two units here are set by hand, and the browser computes their posterior; `postrank` fits no model.

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
validate_postrank_draws(postrank_toy)[c("valid", "jointness_verified", "convergence_verified")]  # TRUE, FALSE, FALSE: the form is checked, jointness and convergence are not
postrank_coefficient_capabilities(pr_tutorial$one)[c("weighted_at_most_G_problem", "minimax_problem")]  # TRUE, FALSE: row "A normal law", first column yes, minimax no
```
:::
